subject: Request: Penetration test report access & redaction approach
messages:
From: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme is moving quickly on the evaluation. Our security team asked if you can share the most recent penetration test report (or an appropriately redacted version) plus an executive summary we can circulate internally. We need the report to validate remediation status for our procurement and compliance review (SOC 2 scope).

A few constraints from our side:
- Report access must be limited to 6 reviewers initially and logged for audit.
- Retention: 30 days maximum on our side unless we request extension.
- Redaction: we can accept exploit PoCs removed but prefer to see vulnerability IDs, severity, and remediation status.

Can you confirm what sharing options you support (redacted PDF vs secure viewer vs on-site review)? Also please flag any evidence artifacts (logs, screenshots) that you cannot provide.

Thanks,
Alex Stevens
Security Lead, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com
[Acme Security]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. High level options we can provide immediately:

1) Redacted PDF (exec summary + selected findings): we can remove exploit step-by-step details and internal IPs, preserve vuln IDs, CVSS, affected component, remediation status and ETA.

2) Secure ephemeral viewer (watermarked, per-user links, view-only, keystroke/audit logging). This preserves more context (stack traces removed) and lets us revoke access if needed.

3) On-site or secure Zoom walkthrough (no file transfer) for highly sensitive artifacts.

We typically pair any of the above with a short remediation status spreadsheet and the SOC 2 artifact bundle (control responses) or SIG/CAIQ mapping upon request. I attached our internal guideline for how we approach executive redaction so you can see examples.

Next steps I suggest: confirm the 6 reviewers (names/emails), whether Acme counsel requires an NDA addendum, and which option you prefer. If you want the secure viewer, we'll need a signed NDA addendum covering limited use and retention.

Att: Redwood_PenTest_ExecGuidelines_v1.0.pdf (guidelines)

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@acme-corp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Looping in a few technical clarifications from infra/security:

- Redaction guidance: we can safely redact exploit PoCs and raw proof-of-concept scripts. We prefer NOT to redact vulnerability identifiers (e.g., internal tracking IDs) or the affected components and severity — those are needed for risk validation.
- Evidence artifacts: some artifacts are derived from customer logs (sanitized); we can provide screenshots and error traces with production identifiers masked. Full raw logs may be restricted unless a separate data-handover agreement is signed.
- Viewer capabilities: our secure viewer supports per-user watermark, IP bounding, download disabled, and access revocation. Audit logs export (CSV) includes viewer identity, timestamp, and page ranges viewed.

If Acme needs a sample redacted page set, we can produce one by EOD Wednesday. Karthik

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Rhee <m.rhee@acme-law.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Thanks — secure viewer sounds ideal. Our initial reviewer list:
- Alex Stevens (me) — alex.stevens@acme-corp.com
- Priya Natarajan — priya@acme-corp.com
- Ben Carter — ben.carter@acme-corp.com
- Legal: Maya Rhee (copied)
- Procurement reviewer: samir.khan@acme-corp.com
- CISO delegate: security@acme-corp.com

We can accept redaction of PoCs; please keep vuln IDs, CVSS, component, remediation status and ETA. We'd like to see a sample redacted exec summary PDF before countersigning any addendum so our counsel can review the language. Can you produce that sample and the proposed NDA addendum?

Also, please confirm retention on Acme side is 30 days and whether your viewer will enforce that or if we need to delete locally.

Alex
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Stevens <alex.stevens@acme-corp.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Maya Rhee <m.rhee@acme-law.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Alex / Maya —

Attached is a draft NDA addendum that: (1) limits use of the information to internal security review, (2) requires deletion/return of all copies after 30 days, (3) prohibits redistribution, (4) allows audit of access logs limited to a summary CSV (no raw logs), and (5) requires mutual notification if further disclosure is requested.

Key points for counsel review:
- We will provide a sample redacted executive summary for review prior to countersignature.
- The addendum includes acceptance criteria for redaction: exploit steps and raw PoC removed; all findings retain IDs, severity, component, remediation status and ETA.
- If Acme requires raw log artifacts, that is escalated to a separate evidence-handover agreement with data minimization controls.

Att: NDA_Addendum_Acme_Redwood_draft.docx

If that looks good, Soojin can send the sample redacted exec summary and the DocuSign link.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pen test report access & executive summary request

Alex / team —

Thanks all. Confirming next steps:
1) I'll upload and share a sample redacted executive summary (PDF) by EOD tomorrow for counsel review — filename will be requested-sample-execsummary-redacted.pdf.
2) Laura will publish the NDA addendum to DocuSign; please route to Maya for countersignature. Link will appear in the related links above.
3) Once countersigned, we'll provision the secure viewer link for the six reviewers with per-user watermarking and a 30-day expiration. The viewer enforces access revocation; local deletion on Acme's side is requested as contractual hygiene.
4) If Acme requests raw logs or deeper evidence, we will open SEC-4232 to track the evidence-handover conversation and required controls.

If you can confirm the reviewer list (as sent earlier) and that counsel has the NDA draft, we'll proceed.

—Soojin
